finding: hx-accordion imports hx-accordion-item as a side-effect import, which auto-registers the sub-component. This is good for DX but means importing hx-accordion always pulls in hx-accordion-item.
suggestion: Document that importing hx-accordion automatically registers hx-accordion-item. This is the correct behavior for Drupal — no action needed.

finding: Uses default slot for hx-accordion-item children. Twig content projects correctly through the slot. Slot validation warns on non-accordion-item children.
suggestion: No action needed. Slot pattern is Drupal-friendly.

finding: Fully declarative — mode attribute controls behavior, no imperative JS needed beyond registration. Works in Twig: <hx-accordion mode="single"><hx-accordion-item>...</hx-accordion-item></hx-accordion>
Uses connectedCallback/disconnectedCallback for event listeners. Properly cleans up on disconnect, safe for Drupal AJAX DOM replacement.
All CSS custom properties use --hx- prefix. No clash risk with Gin/Claro admin themes.
No dynamic imports. Can be loaded from CDN with module scripts.
No form interaction. N/A.

CSS custom property --hx-action-bar-z-index defaults to 10. When position is sticky or bottom, this z-index is active. Drupal admin toolbar (Gin) uses z-index 500+, so no conflict. However, document the z-index token for themers.
suggestion: Document that --hx-action-bar-z-index can be overridden if the action bar needs to layer above or below Drupal admin UI elements.

finding: Uses named slots (start, end, overflow) and a default slot. Slotted Twig content will render correctly. No ::slotted() style concerns since styling is via CSS parts and class-based internal layout.
suggestion: No action needed. Slot-based composition works well with Twig templates.

finding: Fully declarative via attributes (variant, hx-size, position, aria-label). No imperative JS required. Works from Twig with just a script registration tag.
suggestion: Document Twig example: <hx-action-bar aria-label="Patient actions" variant="outlined" position="sticky"><hx-button slot="start">Save</hx-button></hx-action-bar>

finding: Standard Lit component with no dynamic imports. Can be individually imported and tree-shaken.
Event listeners are properly added in connectedCallback and removed in disconnectedCallback. Safe for Drupal AJAX partial page loads.

Alert requires open attribute to be visible. Drupal themers must add open attribute in Twig: <hx-alert variant="warning" open>. Without it, alert is hidden (aria-hidden=true, likely display:none). This is counter-intuitive for new Drupal developers.
suggestion: Document prominently that hx-alert defaults to closed (open=false). Provide Twig template example with open attribute. Consider whether default should be open=true for non-dismissible alerts.

finding: Dismissible alert uses hx-close and hx-after-close CustomEvents. Drupal behaviors need to listen for these events to handle AJAX or state management. Events bubble and are composed, which is correct.
suggestion: Document Drupal.behaviors pattern for listening to hx-close events on dismissible alerts.

finding: Supports default, title, icon, and actions slots. All slots project Twig content correctly through Shadow DOM.
Properly manages ARIA attributes in connectedCallback/disconnectedCallback. Safe for Drupal AJAX re-insertion.
CSS custom properties all use --hx-alert- prefix. No clash with Drupal admin themes.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Size attribute uses hx-size (not size). Drupal themers familiar with standard HTML size attribute may use the wrong name. devWarn catches this at runtime but not at template authoring time.
suggestion: Document the hx-size convention prominently in Drupal integration guide. This applies to all components using hx-size: hx-avatar, hx-badge, hx-counter, hx-icon, hx-progress-bar, hx-progress-ring, hx-spinner, hx-stat, hx-status-indicator, hx-steps, hx-tag, hx-text.

finding: Fully declarative. All properties are attributes: src, alt, initials, hx-size, shape, label. Works in Twig without JS: <hx-avatar src="{{ image }}" alt="{{ name }}" hx-size="lg">
Default slot and badge slot work correctly for Twig content projection.
No event listeners on host. Safe for Drupal AJAX DOM replacement.
CSS custom properties use --hx-avatar- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Fully declarative. All variants controllable via attributes. Works in Twig: <hx-badge variant="error" pill count="5">
Default slot and prefix slot work for Twig content. Count mode bypasses slot.
No host event listeners. Safe for Drupal AJAX.
CSS custom properties use --hx-badge- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Banner uses position: sticky/fixed with z-index: 100. In Drupal admin (Gin/Claro), the admin toolbar has z-index in the hundreds. A fixed banner may layer incorrectly beneath the toolbar.
suggestion: Document that --hx-banner-z-index may need adjustment in Drupal admin context. Provide guidance: --hx-banner-z-index: 501 to sit above Gin toolbar.

finding: Banner defaults to open=true, which is the intuitive default for Drupal themers. Declarative: <hx-banner variant="info" dismissible>System maintenance tonight.</hx-banner>
suggestion: No action needed. Good default for Drupal usage.

finding: Default slot and action slot work for Twig content.
Properly uses connectedCallback/updated lifecycle. Safe for AJAX.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.

json-ld attribute injects a <script> tag directly into document.head. The JSDoc explicitly warns this bypasses Drupal's render pipeline, page cache, BigPipe, and hook_html_head_alter(). Defaults to false which is correct, but Drupal themers may enable it unaware of the consequences.
suggestion: Ensure json-ld defaults to false (confirmed). Add prominent Drupal-specific documentation warning. Provide a server-side Twig template for JSON-LD breadcrumb structured data instead.

finding: hx-breadcrumb uses type-only import for hx-breadcrumb-item. The sub-component is NOT auto-registered when importing hx-breadcrumb alone. Drupal themers must import from the index.ts barrel which exports both.
suggestion: Document that hx-breadcrumb requires hx-breadcrumb-item to be registered. Ensure the per-component library entry point exports both.

finding: Supports explicit current attribute on breadcrumb items for Drupal's breadcrumb system. The component detects consumer-set current attributes and does not override them. This is Drupal-optimized.
suggestion: Document that Drupal themes can set current attribute on the active breadcrumb item explicitly.

finding: Default slot for items, separator slot for custom separators. Works with Twig content.
Properly adds/removes event listeners in connected/disconnectedCallback. Cleans up JSON-LD script on disconnect. Safe for Drupal AJAX.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Button type defaults to 'button' (line 80), not 'submit'. Drupal themers must explicitly set type="submit" in Twig templates for form submission buttons, which is non-obvious.
suggestion: Document the type attribute default prominently in the Drupal integration guide. Provide a Twig snippet: <hx-button type="submit">Save</hx-button>.

finding: Shadow DOM encapsulation is correct for a button component. Slots (default, prefix, suffix) allow Twig-projected content to cross the shadow boundary.
suggestion: No action required. Shadow DOM is appropriate here; slots provide the content injection points Drupal needs.

finding: All public properties (variant, size, disabled, type, href, target, label) are reflected attributes settable from Twig without JS. The hx-size attribute (not 'size') is a Drupal themer awareness item.
suggestion: Document that sizing uses hx-size attribute, not size, in the Twig template reference.

finding: Per-component index.ts re-export exists, enabling tree-shaken imports via a dedicated library entry in mytheme.libraries.yml.
suggestion: No action required. Per-component loading is supported.

finding: No document-level event listeners. Component is self-contained and safe for Drupal AJAX partial re-renders without requiring attach/detach behavior hooks.
suggestion: No action required. Drupal behaviors integration is optional for this component.

finding: Full ElementInternals form association: static formAssociated=true, attachInternals(), form submit via requestSubmit(), formResetCallback, formStateRestoreCallback, formDisabledCallback. Native form submission works without Drupal module coupling.
suggestion: No action required. Form integration is complete.

finding: All visual properties exposed via CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix (--hx-button-bg, --hx-button-color, etc.) and CSS parts (button, label, prefix, suffix). Drupal admin themes can override without touching Shadow DOM.
suggestion: No action required. Theming API is complete.

finding: Component uses ES module imports and @customElement decorator. Compatible with CDN delivery via <script type="module"> in mytheme.libraries.yml.
suggestion: No action required. CDN loading is supported.

finding: Single default slot for hx-button children. Drupal Twig content renders correctly through the slot.
Fully declarative. Orientation, hx-size, and label are all settable via HTML attributes.
Uses ElementInternals for ARIA role. No global event listeners. Safe for AJAX re-attach.
Interactive card uses hx-href attribute (not href) to avoid native HTML collision. Drupal themers may instinctively use href. devWarn does not catch this — the card simply won't be interactive.
suggestion: Document hx-href attribute name prominently. Consider adding a devWarn when href is set instead of hx-href.

finding: Interactive card dispatches hx-click CustomEvent with composed:true. Drupal behaviors need to listen for this event to handle navigation. The card does NOT navigate automatically — the consumer must handle the click.
suggestion: Document Drupal.behaviors pattern: once('wc-card', 'hx-card[hx-href]', context).forEach(card => card.addEventListener('hx-click', e => window.location.href = e.detail.href));

finding: Card uses delegatesFocus: true in shadowRootOptions. This is good for keyboard accessibility but means :focus styles on the host element will be applied when any focusable child inside the shadow root is focused. Drupal themes applying :focus styles to hx-card may see unexpected behavior.
suggestion: Document delegatesFocus behavior for Drupal theme developers. Recommend using ::part(card):focus-visible for styling focus states.

finding: Fully declarative. Multiple named slots (image, heading, footer, actions) map well to Drupal field formatters and Views row templates.
suggestion: No action needed. Excellent Drupal pattern for entity display.

finding: All 5 slots (image, heading, default, footer, actions) properly detect content via slotchange and hide empty containers.
CSS custom properties use --hx-card- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.

Carousel auto-plays when autoplay attribute is set but requires NO imperative JS to cycle slides. Navigation, pagination, and autoplay all work declaratively. However, the goTo/next/previous public methods suggest some use cases need JS.
suggestion: Document that basic carousel works declaratively in Twig. goTo/next/previous are optional for programmatic control.

finding: hx-carousel uses type-only import for hx-carousel-item. The sub-component is NOT auto-registered. Both must be imported via the index.ts barrel.
suggestion: Document that hx-carousel requires hx-carousel-item to be separately registered. Ensure per-component entry point includes both.

finding: Properly cleans up all event listeners, timers, and media query listeners on disconnectedCallback. Safe for Drupal AJAX DOM replacement.
Default slot for carousel items, named slots for custom prev/next buttons. Works with Twig.
CSS custom properties use --hx-carousel- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Shadow DOM with slots for label (default), error, and help-text. JSDoc explicitly documents 'Rich HTML allowed — Drupal can include links in consent labels' for the default slot.
suggestion: No action required. Slot design explicitly supports Drupal content injection patterns.

finding: All public properties (checked, disabled, required, name, value, label, error, helpText, size) are attribute-settable from Twig. Slots accept Drupal Form API rendered labels and errors.
suggestion: No action required. Twig template integration is straightforward.

finding: Per-component index.ts re-export exists for tree-shaken loading.
No document-level event listeners. Self-contained component safe for AJAX re-renders.

Full ElementInternals form association with all four form callbacks (formResetCallback, formStateRestoreCallback, formDisabledCallback, plus setFormValue/setValidity). Name attribute forwarded correctly.
suggestion: No action required. Drupal Form API compatibility is complete.

finding: CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix and CSS parts exposed for admin theme overrides.
ES module compatible. Works with CDN script type=module loading.
JSDoc includes @drupal annotation with a complete Twig example showing proper usage pattern for checkbox group with child hx-checkbox elements. Exemplary Drupal documentation.
suggestion: No action required. This is a model for other components to follow.

finding: Shadow DOM with default slot for child hx-checkbox elements. Twig templates project checkbox children through the slot.
Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Syncs name and disabled state to child checkboxes via slot change observation. Re-inserted children during AJAX partial replacement will be re-synced automatically.
suggestion: No action required. Child syncing handles Drupal AJAX scenarios.

finding: Multi-value form submission via FormData. Each checked checkbox value is appended. formResetCallback unchecks all children. Name propagation to children is automatic.
CSS custom properties and parts exposed for theme overrides.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

Copy button uses navigator.clipboard.writeText which requires HTTPS. Drupal staging/dev environments often use HTTP. The component handles this gracefully (catch block), but the copy-to-clipboard silently fails on HTTP.
suggestion: Document that copy functionality requires HTTPS (secure context). The hx-copy event still fires, so Drupal behaviors can implement a fallback copy mechanism.

finding: Slot content is extracted as text only — HTML markup is stripped. JSDoc documents this but Drupal CKEditor output or Twig markup in the slot will lose its HTML formatting.
suggestion: Document that only plain text code is supported. Pre-highlighted HTML from Drupal's code filter modules will be stripped to text.

finding: Declarative: <hx-code-snippet language="php" copyable max-lines="10">{{ code }}</hx-code-snippet>
No host event listeners. Timer cleanup on disconnect. Safe for Drupal AJAX.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Shadow DOM is appropriate, but the swatches property has attribute: false because arrays cannot be set via HTML attributes. This means swatches must be set imperatively via JavaScript.
suggestion: Document a Drupal behaviors pattern that reads swatches from a data-swatches attribute containing JSON and sets the property. The component JSDoc already documents this pattern — ensure it is in the Starlight docs.

finding: Most properties are attribute-settable, but swatches (array) requires JS initialization. Twig can set data-swatches as a JSON string attribute, but a Drupal behavior must parse and apply it.
suggestion: Provide a complete Twig + behavior example: <hx-color-picker data-swatches='{{ swatches|json_encode }}'> paired with a Drupal.behaviors handler that parses the data attribute.

finding: Adds document-level pointermove, pointerup, and click listeners in connectedCallback with bound references stored for cleanup in disconnectedCallback. This is AJAX-safe — Drupal's attach/detach lifecycle will trigger proper cleanup.
suggestion: No action required. Listener lifecycle is properly managed for Drupal AJAX contexts. Document this as a positive pattern.

finding: Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Full ElementInternals form association. Submits hex color string as form value.
CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix exposed for admin theme overrides.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.
The labelRemoveOption property has attribute: false (it is a function for i18n). Cannot be set from Twig. Requires a Drupal behavior to set the removal label callback for internationalized sites.
suggestion: Provide a Drupal behaviors example that sets labelRemoveOption via JS. For non-i18n sites, the default English label works without JS.

finding: Shadow DOM with named 'option' slot for slotted <option> elements. Twig templates provide options as standard HTML option elements projected through the slot.
suggestion: No action required. Slotted option pattern is Drupal-friendly.

finding: Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Document-level click listener added in connectedCallback and removed in disconnectedCallback. This is AJAX-safe — proper lifecycle management for Drupal's DOM manipulation patterns.
suggestion: No action required. Listener cleanup is correct.

finding: Full ElementInternals form association with setFormValue, setValidity, and all form callbacks.
CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix and CSS parts exposed.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.
Fully declarative layout primitive. <hx-container width="content" padding="lg"><slot content here></hx-container>. No JS needed beyond registration.
suggestion: No action needed. Ideal for Drupal page templates.

finding: Default slot for any content. No special slot requirements.
No event listeners, no state. Stateless layout component. Safe for AJAX.
CSS custom properties use --hx-container- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.

The value attribute must be set from Twig to specify what to copy. The copy action itself is handled internally via navigator.clipboard.writeText. Works declaratively but requires HTTPS context for clipboard API.
suggestion: Document that clipboard API requires HTTPS. In local Drupal dev (HTTP), the hx-copy-error event will fire. Provide a Twig example: <hx-copy-button value="{{ patient_id }}">Copy ID</hx-copy-button>

finding: Proper disconnectedCallback cleanup of feedback timer. Safe for AJAX page loads.

Counter animation starts automatically on connectedCallback — no imperative JS needed. However, the animation runs immediately when the element enters the DOM. In Drupal Views or AJAX-loaded content, this means the animation fires every time content is injected, which may not be desired.
suggestion: Document that animation triggers on DOM insertion. For Drupal AJAX contexts, the counter re-animates each time. Consider adding an attribute to disable animation on reconnect.

finding: Respects prefers-reduced-motion. Cancels requestAnimationFrame on disconnect. Safe for Drupal AJAX.
Declarative: <hx-counter value="1234" prefix="$" suffix="+" hx-size="lg" duration="2000">
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
CSS custom properties use --hx-counter- prefix. No clash risk.
No slots. Counter renders its own value. N/A for light DOM concerns.

columns and rows properties are type: Array. Lit's default converter does NOT JSON-parse array attributes. However, this component explicitly handles JSON string coercion in willUpdate (lines 165-188), parsing string values from attributes. This is Drupal-friendly but requires Twig to output valid JSON strings, which means escaping is critical.
suggestion: Document Twig pattern carefully: columns='{{ columns_json|e('html_attr') }}' rows='{{ rows_json|e('html_attr') }}'. Single quotes around attribute values are essential since JSON contains double quotes. Provide a working Drupal Views integration example.

finding: hx-data-table renders its own table structure in Shadow DOM from the columns/rows data properties. It does NOT use slots for table rows. Drupal-rendered table content cannot be projected into the table body. Only toolbar, empty, and loading slots accept light DOM content.
suggestion: For Drupal Views that render table rows server-side, use hx-table (slot-based composition) instead of hx-data-table. hx-data-table is designed for client-side data binding via JSON. Document this distinction clearly.

finding: DevWarn fires when rows > 500. Drupal Views with many results should use server-side pagination. The page and page-size attributes enable client-side pagination but the full dataset must still be passed as JSON.
suggestion: Document that for large Drupal datasets, prefer server-side pagination and pass only the current page of rows. Listen to hx-sort and hx-page-change events in Drupal.behaviors to trigger AJAX refreshes.

finding: Shadow DOM with slots for label, error, help-text, prefix, suffix. Calendar popup rendered in shadow DOM.
All primary properties (value, min, max, locale, label, name, required, disabled, error, helpText, size) are attribute-settable from Twig.
Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Document-level click and keydown listeners created in connectedCallback with bound handler references, removed in disconnectedCallback. Properly handles re-connection. AJAX-safe.
suggestion: No action required. Exemplary lifecycle management.

finding: Full ElementInternals form association. Date value submitted as ISO string. All form callbacks implemented.
CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix and CSS parts exposed. Locale property supports Drupal's multilingual date formatting.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

hx-dialog has show(), showModal(), and close() imperative methods. While the open attribute exists and can be set declaratively, opening a modal dialog purely from Twig requires JS to call showModal() on the native <dialog> element inside Shadow DOM. Setting open="true" in Twig markup will open the dialog on page load, which is rarely desired.
suggestion: Document the Drupal.behaviors pattern shown in the component's own JSDoc (lines 58-69). The pattern uses data-hx-dialog-trigger attribute convention. This is the recommended Drupal integration path.

finding: The open property is reflected and can be used declaratively to show the dialog on initial render. For Drupal use cases like server-rendered confirmation dialogs, this works: <hx-dialog open heading="Confirm">. However, modal body scroll lock and focus trap activate immediately.
suggestion: Document that open attribute is available for SSR scenarios but most Drupal use cases should wire trigger buttons via Drupal.behaviors. Provide both patterns in docs.

finding: Uses lockBodyScroll/unlockBodyScroll utilities with reference counting. If the dialog element is removed from DOM during an AJAX partial page replacement while open, disconnectedCallback calls unlockBodyScroll. This is safe. However, if Drupal's BigPipe replaces a region containing a dialog trigger, the trigger reference is lost.
suggestion: Document that dialog triggers should NOT be placed inside BigPipe-replaced regions, or use event delegation in Drupal.behaviors with context parameter to re-wire triggers after AJAX.

finding: Dialog uses z-index via --hx-z-index-modal (default 100). Drupal admin toolbar (Gin/Claro) uses z-index 500+. The native <dialog> element's top layer in modal mode should stack above the toolbar, but non-modal dialogs may appear behind the admin toolbar.
suggestion: Document that non-modal dialogs may need --hx-z-index-modal increased (e.g., to 600) when used alongside Drupal admin themes. Modal dialogs use the browser's top layer and are unaffected.

finding: Fully declarative. <hx-divider orientation="horizontal" spacing="md" decorative>. Optional label via slot or attribute.
Default slot for optional label text. Works with Twig content.
No host event listeners. Safe for Drupal AJAX.
CSS custom properties use --hx-divider- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.

hx-drawer requires imperative show()/hide() methods to open and close. The open attribute is reflected and can be set declaratively, but setting open in Twig markup opens the drawer on page load. A Drupal.behaviors pattern is needed to wire trigger buttons.

Drawer adds aria-hidden to sibling elements of document.body when open (line 376). If Drupal admin toolbar is a sibling of body, it will be hidden from screen readers while the drawer is open. This is correct ARIA behavior for a modal, but document this for Drupal themers.
suggestion: Document that hx-drawer operates as a modal overlay that hides background content from assistive technology. This is intentional ARIA behavior. The contained attribute disables this for non-modal drawer usage.

finding: Adds document-level keydown listener in _addListeners(). Removes in _removeListeners() and disconnectedCallback. If the element is removed from DOM via AJAX while the drawer is open, disconnectedCallback fires and cleans up. Safe.

Imports @floating-ui/dom as a static ES module import. When loaded from CDN, this dependency must be bundled into the component's output file or available as a separate module. If the CDN serves unbundled source, the import path will fail.
suggestion: Ensure the CDN build bundles @floating-ui/dom into the component output. Document that per-component CDN loading requires the floating-ui dependency to be resolved.

finding: Adds document-level click listener with capture:true for outside-click detection. Properly removes in disconnectedCallback and _hide(). However, on Drupal AJAX partial page replacement, if the dropdown is open and gets removed, the document listener is cleaned up. If a new dropdown instance is added by AJAX, it will register its own listener. Safe.
suggestion: No action needed for standard Drupal AJAX. For Drupal.behaviors detach, no special handling is required since disconnectedCallback handles cleanup.

finding: Panel z-index defaults to 1000 via --hx-dropdown-panel-z-index. Drupal admin toolbar z-index is 500+. The dropdown panel will render above the toolbar, which may be desired or problematic depending on context.
suggestion: Document that --hx-dropdown-panel-z-index can be adjusted. In admin contexts, dropdowns inside the content area should work correctly since they use fixed positioning.

finding: The open attribute is reflected and can be set declaratively. However, opening a dropdown typically requires user interaction (click on trigger). Twig renders the trigger element in the trigger slot and menu items in the default slot. Works well with Twig.
suggestion: Document Twig example with slot usage.

finding: Shadow DOM wrapper that injects light-DOM <span> elements for ARIA describedby bridging across the shadow boundary. This bridge pattern solves a real Drupal problem: screen readers need to associate shadow DOM controls with light DOM help/error text.
suggestion: Document the ARIA bridge pattern in the Drupal integration guide as a reference for custom field wrappers.

finding: Slots for control (default), label, help-text, error. All act as layout containers — Twig projects field elements through slots.
Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Label click handler programmatically focuses the slotted control. Works with Drupal-rendered controls.
Not form-associated (by design). Pure layout wrapper. Skips ARIA bridging for HX-* elements that manage their own ARIA.
suggestion: No action required. This is correctly not form-associated.

finding: CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix and CSS parts exposed.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

The for attribute has a documented limitation: a label rendered inside Shadow DOM cannot natively associate with a light DOM input via for/id. The component documents a workaround using aria-labelledby with the host element's ID.
suggestion: Document this limitation prominently in the Drupal integration guide. Recommend using hx-field wrapper or aria-labelledby pattern instead of relying on for attribute for cross-boundary association.

finding: Properties (for, required) are attribute-settable from Twig. Default slot accepts label text.
Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
No document-level event listeners. Self-contained.
Not form-associated (by design). Presentational label component.
CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix exposed.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

The setProgress() public method for upload progress indication requires imperative JS. Drupal modules handling file uploads via AJAX will need a Drupal behavior to call this method during upload progress.
suggestion: Document a Drupal behaviors example that listens for Drupal.ajax progress events and calls element.setProgress(percent) on the hx-file-upload component.

finding: Shadow DOM with slots for label, help-text, error. Drag-and-drop zone and hidden file input in shadow DOM.
Public properties (name, accept, multiple, maxFileSize, maxFiles, disabled, required, label, helpText, error) are all attribute-settable from Twig.
Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Full ElementInternals form association. Multi-file FormData submission. formStateRestoreCallback correctly clears files since File objects cannot be serialized to form state.
CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix exposed.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

getFormElements() contains a hardcoded allowlist of only 6 component tag names. Newer form components (hx-date-picker, hx-time-picker, hx-color-picker, hx-file-upload, hx-number-input, hx-slider, hx-rating, hx-toggle-button, hx-combobox) are NOT included. This means hx-form's validation orchestration and setErrors() will silently skip these components.
suggestion: Replace the hardcoded allowlist with a dynamic check: query all children with ElementInternals form association (static formAssociated === true) or use a shared interface/attribute marker. At minimum, add the missing 9 component tags to the allowlist immediately.

finding: POSITIVE: Uses Light DOM via createRenderRoot() returning this. This is the optimal pattern for Drupal — Twig-rendered content is not isolated by Shadow DOM. AdoptedStylesheetsController provides scoped CSS without Shadow DOM encapsulation. This is the gold-standard Drupal integration pattern.
suggestion: No action required. Document this as the reference pattern for any future Light DOM components.

finding: When action attribute is set, renders a <form> wrapper. When no action, renders only <slot> so Drupal's own <form> tag from Form API wraps the content. This dual mode perfectly accommodates both standalone and Drupal Form API usage.
suggestion: No action required. Document both modes in the Drupal integration guide.

finding: Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
Listens for native submit and reset events on its own DOM. No document-level listeners. Safe for Drupal AJAX.
Light DOM means Drupal admin theme CSS applies directly without Shadow DOM barriers. CSS custom properties still available for targeted overrides.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

Locale detection falls back to document.documentElement.lang, then navigator.language. Drupal sets the lang attribute on html based on the active language. This means hx-format-date automatically respects Drupal's language settings.
suggestion: Document that hx-format-date inherits locale from Drupal's html lang attribute. No additional configuration needed for multilingual Drupal sites.

finding: Fully declarative. All formatting options are HTML attributes. Renders a semantic time element. Excellent for Drupal date fields.
suggestion: Document Twig patterns for common Drupal date field scenarios.

finding: No slots. Renders only a time element in Shadow DOM. No light DOM content needed.
No external dependencies beyond Lit and @helixui/tokens. Small component, excellent for tree-shaking.
Fully declarative layout primitive. <hx-grid columns="3" gap="lg">. Works with Drupal Views grids.
suggestion: No action needed. Document as replacement for Views grid format.

finding: Default slot for grid children. hx-grid-item is optional for explicit placement.
No event listeners. Stateless layout. Safe for AJAX.
CSS custom properties use --hx-grid- prefix. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
Shadow DOM with default slot for help text content. Simple presentational component with variant icons.
Properties (variant) are attribute-settable from Twig. Default slot accepts text content.
Per-component index.ts re-export exists.
No document-level event listeners. Self-contained.
Not form-associated (by design). Presentational help text component.
CSS custom properties with --hx- prefix exposed.
ES module compatible for CDN delivery.

Inline fetch mode (src attribute) requires JavaScript and fetch() to render the SVG. Before hydration, nothing is visible. For Drupal SSR/BigPipe, this causes content shift. The JSDoc already recommends sprite mode for Drupal.
suggestion: Document that Drupal themes MUST use sprite mode (name + sprite-url attributes), not inline fetch mode (src). Sprite mode renders via <svg><use> which works without JS.

finding: Inline mode fetches SVG files from URLs. When using CDN, the SVG files must be on the same CDN or CORS must be configured. Module-level _svgCache persists across page lifetime, which is good for performance.
suggestion: Document CORS requirements for inline SVG mode when icons are on a different CDN origin than the page.

finding: Uses unsafeHTML to render fetched SVG content. The component sanitizes the SVG (strips scripts, event handlers, dangerous URIs), but Drupal security teams may flag unsafeHTML usage during security review.

Navigation items must be passed as a JSON array via the items attribute. The component has a custom converter (lines 66-78) that JSON-parses the attribute value. All navigation rendering happens in Shadow DOM from this data. No slots for nav items.

finding: hx-nav renders ALL navigation markup in Shadow DOM from the items property. There are NO slots for navigation items. Drupal's menu system renders <ul>/<li>/<a> elements server-side, but none of this content can be projected into hx-nav.
suggestion: For Drupal sites that need server-rendered navigation HTML (for SEO, no-JS fallback), hx-nav is NOT suitable. Consider hx-top-nav (slot-based) instead, or provide a Drupal module that serializes the menu tree to JSON for hx-nav. Document this limitation prominently.

finding: The component calls e.preventDefault() on all item clicks (line 163), then dispatches hx-nav-select. Drupal.behaviors must listen for hx-nav-select to handle navigation (e.g., window.location.href = e.detail.item.href). Links do NOT navigate natively.
suggestion: Document that hx-nav intercepts all clicks and requires a Drupal.behaviors event listener for actual page navigation. This is a critical integration detail.

finding: Fully declarative. All configuration via HTML attributes (total-pages, current-page, sibling-count, etc.). The component even includes a Twig example in its JSDoc (lines 47-63) with Drupal pager integration notes.

finding: Default z-index is 9999 via --hx-popover-z-index. This is higher than Drupal's admin toolbar (500+) and will stack above it. For popovers inside admin content areas, this is correct. For popovers that should appear below the toolbar, this needs adjustment.
suggestion: Document --hx-popover-z-index. The default 9999 is intentionally high for overlay content but can be reduced for specific Drupal admin contexts.

finding: Adds document-level click and keydown listeners while open. Clears them in disconnectedCallback and _hide(). The _showTimer is also cleaned up. Safe for AJAX lifecycle.

finding: Low-level positioning primitive. Can be used declaratively via anchor slot and active attribute. The component includes a Twig example in its JSDoc (lines 102-113) and a Drupal.behaviors example (lines 116-128).

finding: The accessibility contract section (lines 67-80) clearly states that hx-popup provides NO ARIA semantics. Consumers must add role, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and focus management themselves. This is a significant burden for Drupal themers.

finding: Default z-index is 9000 via --hx-popup-z-index. High enough to stack above most Drupal content but below hx-popover (9999) and hx-tooltip (9999).
suggestion: Document the z-index hierarchy across floating components for Drupal admin theme compatibility.

finding: Component warns (devWarn) when label is missing. In Drupal production, devWarn may be suppressed. This is an invisible accessibility failure — the progressbar has no name in the a11y tree.

finding: The toast-factory appends hx-toast-stack to document.body. On Drupal AJAX page loads, these stacks persist since they are on document.body, not inside replaced regions. The factory checks for existing stacks via querySelector before creating new ones. Safe for Drupal AJAX.

finding: Fully declarative and slot-based. Unlike hx-nav (data-driven), hx-top-nav accepts Drupal-rendered menu HTML in slots. This is the preferred component for Drupal menu integration.
suggestion: Document as the recommended navigation component for Drupal. Server-rendered menu links go in the default slot.

finding: Traverses light DOM children recursively to find visible items. If tree items are added/removed via Drupal AJAX, the slotchange handler re-initializes roving tabindex. Safe for dynamic content.
Default slot for hx-tree-item children. The component traverses light DOM children to build the visible item list. Twig can render nested hx-tree-item elements.
Fully declarative. label and selection attributes control behavior. Tree structure is built from nested hx-tree-item elements in light DOM.
suggestion: Document Twig pattern for rendering hierarchical Drupal taxonomy or menu trees as hx-tree-item elements.

finding: Declarative utility. <hx-visually-hidden>Screen reader text</hx-visually-hidden>. focusable attribute for skip links.
Default slot for hidden content. Works with Twig.
No event listeners. Safe for AJAX.
No custom CSS properties exposed. No clash risk.
No dynamic imports. CDN-compatible.
